units.review:
Cosmic Yui is a single-target Nuclear damage dealer who uses All-Out Attack damage as her main damage multiplier. Although the explanation may seem complicated, the actual gameplay cycle is simple. If you just follow the rotation order without worrying too much about the details, it works smoothly.

- At the start of each turn, 1 Veggie Knight is automatically summoned, and using Veggie Knights, Go! (1T cooldown) also summons 1 Veggie Knight.
  - Eggplant → Potato → Mushroom → Asparagus

- When using Veg-Out Attack, if you have 2 or more Potato Knights, additional Potato Knights will be consumed to increase damage. (At least 1 Potato Knight will remain.)

- 『Veggie Energy』: At 7 stacks, the passive activates the damage effect of Veg-Out Attack automatically.

units.tagsKr: 추가 턴, 주원
units.review:
The protagonist of Persona 5, Ren fights alongside his initial Persona, Arsène, as an **AoE Curse dealer**.

By stacking three Will of Rebellion stacks gained through his skills and passives, he immediately performs an **Extra Turn** at the end of the turn and gains increased damage.

His Skill 1 and Skill 2, as well as his HIGHLIGHT, all generate Will of Rebellion stacks. Skill 1 is an AoE attack suited for multiple enemies, while Skill 2 is a single-target skill for isolated foes.

Since Extra Actions also generate HIGHLIGHT gauge and reduce the cooldown of his Elucidator Thief skill, he can form highly flexible and creative tactical loops depending on the situation.

units.review:
A SP-based buffer **specialized in boosting CRIT DMG**. Consumes all SP with Skill 3 to increase an ally’s CRIT Rate, then grants ATK and CRIT DMG buffs based on the amount of SP consumed. As a character that provides a massive amount of buffs, it has been **one of the best buffers** and a consistent staple pick in parties since release. Strategist Thief tends to stay relevant for a long time, so if you have spare resources, it’s strongly recommended to add them to your lineup.
To get the most value out of Skill 3, it’s important to recover SP to the cap. At Awareness 0, the maximum SP is 200. SP recovery naturally restores 10 at the start of each turn, and SP Recovery is **rounded up**, meaning both a 9.9% increase and a 0.1% increase result in the same +1 (based on 10 SP recovered). Considering that Skill 1 and Skill 2 each additionally restore 16 SP, **you need 450.1% SP Recovery to restore 200 SP within 2 turns.** > **Required SP Recovery for Revelation sub-stats (excluding Thieves Den): 31.2%** > ※ Base stats/188.5% + Awareness 0/60% + Revelation main stat/90.4% + Revelation set bonus/80% = 418.9%
If the ally targeted by Skill 3 deals skill damage **5 times or more within 2 turns**, the passive triggers, and the maximum effect requires **10 or more hits**. Because of this, it synergizes well with multi-hit DPS characters, and since Passive 3 has **no cap**, it’s best to stack **as much CRIT DMG as possible.**
At Awareness 0, Skill 1 applies only to Wind element allies, but at Awareness 1 it applies to all elements, and it also increases the CRIT DMG received, giving it much broader versatility.

units.review:
A Physical-support buffer specialized in Pierce. She gains Velocity stacks whenever any Phantom Thief finishes their action.

When enough Velocity stacks are accumulated, she enters an Extra Action. After entering an Extra Action, her buffs become enhanced: Skill 1 gains guaranteed Critical hits, Skill 2 grants a shield, and Skill 3 provides amplified Piercing effects.

With Resonance 1 or higher, Velocity generation becomes smoother, enabling her to enter an Extra Action roughly every two turns.

Although she was released before the Pierce mechanic rework, the attribute received significant buffs afterward, causing her value to skyrocket.

Beyond Pierce itself, she provides highly useful buffs such as Attack, Damage Bonus, and even HIGHLIGHT, giving her **excellent versatility and strong overall performance**.

To make full use of her kit, **her Speed stat must be raised significantly**, which can be challenging to achieve. 

Additionally, to utilize the effect of reducing DOWN values through Skill 1's Critical, it is important to pay attention to Critical Rate as well.

As a special note, Mayumi's Highlight lasts 2 turns, or 3 turns at Awareness 4+ (A4+), but it has a slightly unusual interaction. 

For convenience, the community sometimes refers to this as "2.1 turns" or "3.1 turns." This does not mean there is literally an extra 0.1 turn.

If Highlight is applied immediately before an ally takes an action, the buff's remaining duration will not decrease after that action, so using it right before your main attacker acts lets you effectively play it as if it had 1 extra turn of value.

units.review:
Dual-attribute Phantom Thief idol and a single-target Wind/Ice dealer. Although she has dual attributes, **Wind is effectively the only attribute** that sees practical use. Skill 3 deploys a field, and the core mechanic is **building stacks through allies’ same-attribute attacks, then detonating those stacks on the next turn alongside her own attack to deal heavy damage**. The number of hits from allies’ same-attribute attacks does not matter. Even if an ally deals five instances of damage with a single Wind attack, it still builds only 1 stack.
Revelation choices vary depending on the situation. The **Medi.+Opul.** set is chosen when you gain the DEF reduction effect at Awareness 2 or higher, or when you already have a high amount of Pierce. It’s also a good option when your party includes a character with a powerful DEF reduction effect (e.g., HOWLER), making the **Free.+Triu.** card set’s Pierce effect effectively meaningless. Since Wonder can continuously deal Wind damage while reducing DEF, use a DEF calculator to determine the best setup for your specific situation.

A **TECHNICAL-focused AoE DEF Down debuffer specialized in Burn setups**.

She gains her unique stacks at the start of her turn and when using Skill 1, and once she reaches 4 stacks, her Skill 3 becomes significantly enhanced.

As the first character to introduce TECHNICAL-type effects, she uses the Ice Technical effect: when dealing TECHNICAL damage to a Burned enemy, she can inflict a 2-turn effect that increases the Fire/Ice damage the target receives.

**Skill 1 grants “Technical Precision” when attacking a Burned enemy, enhancing her TECHNICAL effects.**  
Because of this, **inflicting Burn on at least one enemy is crucial**, leading players to frequently rely on Fire Item Charms or the Persona **Throne**.

Technical Precision: Influences the potency of additional TECHNICAL effects. For every 100 points gained (values below 100 scale proportionally):  
- “Fireburn”: Skill damage bonus increases by 10%.  
- “Short Circuit”: Skill damage bonus increases by 10%.  
- “Iceburn”: Fire/Ice damage taken increases by 5%.  
- “Windburn”: Additional damage increases by 6%.  
- “Deepfreeze”: Base activation rate increases by 2.5%.

For a detailed understanding of this mechanism, please refer to the guide: [TECHNICAL Enhancement - Technical Precision](/en/article/technical-master/)

units.review:
An awakened form of a Phantom Thief member. **A tank who provides shields to allies and designates one ally to take HP consumption and damage on their behalf.**

Compared to other Defense-role Phantom Thieves in the same position, he possesses higher buff values, allowing him to provide both stability and increased damage output.

When his HP is 20,000 or higher, every Persona skill used each turn loads his Gun attack, applying a 40% DEF reduction. His signature weapon also reduces enemy DEF, allowing him to function as a competent debuffer.

His ability to take HP consumption on behalf of allies is designed to synergize with the simultaneously awakened Shoki Ikenami, replacing the HP cost of Shoki’s Skill 2 and increasing the enhancement value of Skill 3.

All attack skills are guaranteed critical hits, allowing Critical Rate to be excluded from stat options. Since his damage scales based on HP, ATK can also be excluded from stat investment.

As a special note, although Gunslinger Shun's Highlight lasts 4 turns, it follows the same mechanic as Mayumi's Highlight.

For convenience, the community sometimes refers to this as "4.1 turns." This does not mean there is literally an extra 0.1 turn.

If Highlight is applied immediately before an ally takes an action, the buff's remaining duration will not decrease after that action, so using it right before your main attacker acts lets you effectively play it as if it had 1 extra turn of value.

Ayaka Sakai is a buffer who specializes in controlling HIGHLIGHT (HL). All characters normally require four actions to reuse HL, meaning that in a standard six-turn boss fight, HL can typically be used twice—once on turn 2 and once on turn 6. However, **her Skill 3 forces a powered-up HL activation regardless of cooldown**, completely disrupting the existing HL cycle.
Her Skill 2 increases an ally’s Attack, and once upgraded with Ascension 1, it also grants a 15% Critical Rate buff, making it quite efficient. Ayaka’s HL provides buffs to the team while increasing HL charge generation for a duration, allowing the party to maintain the usual HL cycle while potentially gaining an extra HL use through Ayaka’s own HL.
Her Signature Weapon **starts battles with a large amount of HL gauge**, allowing her to trigger HL very early. When **fully enhanced to R5**, it provides 76% HL gauge. Combined with the Revelation set that gives an additional 25%, **she can activate HL immediately upon entering battle**. For this reason, the unusual build of **A1R5** has become recognized as a highly efficient upgrade path for her.

units.review:
Designed as a **counter-type damage dealer based on Defense**, this character excels as a **durable or auto-play optimized dealer**.

Due to the unstable **65% counter rate**, unless Skill 3 guaranteed 100% counter or the Highlight is used, repeated runs may be necessary to achieve the highest score.

Since most characters scale with ATK and many buffers boost ATK, **available buff options are limited**.

Because it is a **counter-type dealer**, unlike other dealers who are placed last in the turn order, it is more effective to **assign them to the first slot** in terms of maintaining buffs.

Though Penetration is granted through passives and Awareness 6, Surt and Jack-o-Lantern, intended for FOX, have low base Defense, making it difficult to see dramatic results.

---

With the LV100 expansion, his new passive effects **largely fix the long-standing issue of being too dependent on pure Defense scaling.** Up to 90% of his Attack is now converted into Defense, letting him benefit from ATK buffs as well, and the increase to his core counterattack damage plus the powerful Ice-team buffs granted through [Silver Frost] stacks make him feel almost like a different character.

Because this passive structure affects all Ice allies, pairing him with Miyu·Summer, who used to compete for a similar slot, lets him build [Silver Frost] stacks very quickly, and he has now grown into a unit that can justify his slot even on his own.

Additionally, in Asia version 5.0, he was moved from the limited pool into the standard pool.

units.review:
A powerful single-target DPS that applies stacks of the Curse-element DoT Lovesick to enemies. Applies Lovesick to enemies through S1 and S2, then after reaching maximum stacks, **refreshes the duration with S3 and deals heavy damage**. **Highlight is Ichigo's core skill, activating stacked Lovesick effects and allowing Lovesick to crit.**
Ichigo is extremely powerful, but her damage-dealing mechanism is the most complex among all characters to date. Lovesick deals damage in two main ways: damage dealt at the end of the enemy’s turn and forced DoT activation via Highlight. - **Each Lovesick stack snapshots Ichigo’s buff state at the time of application, and when refreshed via S3, it overwrites with Ichigo’s buffs at that moment.** - DoT counts as neither a Persona skill nor a Resonance, so it is unaffected by Stable Domain; Crit Mult is applied only when a critical hit occurs. - For end-of-turn DoT settlement, Ichigo’s pierce buffs do not apply, making Defense Reduction effects more significant compared to other characters.
Below is the buff table showing which of Ichigo’s buffs apply: | - | ATK / Damage Mult | Crit Rate / Crit Mult | DEF Reduction | Pierce | |---------------------------|----------------------|------------------------------|---------------|--------| | S1/S2/S3 | O | O | O | O | | Lovesick Application/Refresh | O | - | O | - | | Lovesick×2 Activation - Highlight | - | O (based on activation time) | - | - | | DoT Activation - Highlight | - | - | - | - | | Lovesick Activation - Turn End | - | O (based on activation time) | - | - | | Highlight Base | O | - | O | O | ※ It is currently unconfirmed whether pierce rate applies to DoT activations triggered by Highlight.
The **DoT Damage Increase** buff is calculated in a separate bucket from standard damage increases. For reference, Nian’s DoT Damage Increase, released before Ichigo, is calculated in the standard damage increase bucket.

units.review:
An original P5R character who acts as a single-target Bless dealer centered around HIGHLIGHT. Her gimmicks are complex and her damage is built around HIGHLIGHT, so including Ayaka Sakai in the party is essentially mandatory. When the conditions are met, however, she can **deliver damage beyond expectations.** The goal is to **use Skill 2 once and Skill 1 three times to build a total of 4 stacks, then trigger an empowered HL**. Even if you use Skill 2, Skill 1 will automatically trigger when allies take actions, so it’s also possible to use Skill 2 in place of Skill 1.
From Awareness 1 onward, Skill 2’s duration is extended by 1 turn, causing allies to automatically trigger Skill 1 twice, which lets her use HIGHLIGHT on turn 3 with all 4 stacks fully built regardless of the ally lineup. Skill 3 has relatively high scaling, so even at Awareness 0, using Skill 3 can sometimes result in higher overall damage in the rotation, even if HIGHLIGHT has only 3 stacks charged on turn 3. units.review:
Debuffer who can **greatly reduce Down Points regardless of enemy weaknesses and increase the damage taken by Downed enemies**. - Skill 1: Applies [DEF Down] and [Damage Taken Up] for 2 turns, and unlocks Skill 3. - Skill 3: **Reduces Down Points by 5**, strengthens “Down Special Attack” and [Damage Taken Up] for 1 turn, and also **enhances the next Skill 2**. - Skill 2: When enhanced, reduces Down Points by 4 and applies a 1-turn debuff.
Quickly builds up Down and enhances the **independent bucket 『Down Special Attack』**. Since this buff stacks separately, you can always expect a certain level of damage enhancement. However, some limitations exist as listed below, so it's advisable to refer to them when operating. - AoE bosses have a base Down value of 5, making Skill 2 unable to guarantee Down before A1. Single-target bosses have even higher Down values, lowering her effectiveness further. - Although she has multiple self-buffs (passives/skills), enemies stand up at the end of their turn, removing the debuffs—making it difficult for her to benefit from them. - DEF Down is tied to HL, causing **forced HL usage**. - Her 4★ weapon activates when enemies are Downed, but without A1 the efficiency drops sharply—making the **3★ weapon** a reasonable alternative.

units.review:
A single-target Physical attacker who switches between **Doctor** and **Ripper** modes, stacking **Bleed** and detonating it through **Rending** damage. From **Awareness 0–1**, Kira focuses on building and maintaining Bleed stacks as a “Bleed-type”; from **Awareness 6**, he transitions into a “Burst-type” that repeatedly triggers **Rending**. Burst-oriented play becomes viable starting from Awareness 1.
**A0–A1 (Bleed-type)** Focus on stacking and refreshing **Bleed** in **Doctor mode**. - Use S1 → HL to apply 5 stacks → maintain with S2 → enter **Ripper mode** briefly at the end of turn.
**A6 (Burst-type)** Focus on repeatedly triggering **Rending** in **Ripper mode**. - After reaching 13 **Bleed** stacks, activate **Nightfall** → chain S1/S2 to trigger **Rending** bursts. --- **Mindscape Core Activation** Kira gained a skill that, at the end of each foe's turn, permanently decreases that foe's max HP by 1.25% for each **Bleed** stack, up to 50%. **At 10 stacks, Kira can reduce any boss's HP by 50% over 5 turns**, greatly improving his general usability. He also gained a passive that lets him double as either a damage-over-time sub-DPS or a sub-DPS paired with Physical damage dealers.
With Mindscape Core activation, Kira received multiple buffs and system-level reworks. **All damage dealt by his Persona skills and HIGHLIGHT is now treated as damage over time**, allowing it to benefit from every buff related to “damage over time amp.” In addition, the **Rending damage dealt by S2 can now critically hit**, improving the value of critical rate and critical damage buffs, which had previously been one of Kira's limitations. ※ After this patch, critical damage and critical rate have become much more valuable in Kira builds. The HP-scaling damage reduction effects previously held by bosses were also removed. Instead, the limit was changed to an Attack-scaling cap, giving **Bleed** damage real value in competitive content.

She is an AoE Psy dealer who originally appeared in P5.

units.review:
Phoebe is an Elucidator Phantom Thief who provides a powerful elemental damage bonus, making her more valuable the more allies share her element. Each time an ally performs an elemental attack, she gains 1 stack of that element, and **when 3 stacks are reached, she mixes a cocktail**. **The more stacks of the same element gathered, the higher the quality of the cocktail produced**. Even if a low-quality cocktail is created, one can be upgraded to the highest tier via Skill 2, and **Skill 3 can greatly boost the damage of a specific element**.
Her exclusive weapon not only increases ATK but also has an effect that can alter turn order, so it’s worth investing in. As the first 5★ Elucidator Phantom Thief, unlike 4★ units who shared 15% of their stats with allies, **she shares 20% of her stats with allies, making her own stats even more important**. Being a cocktail-dependent character, at Awareness 6, the cocktail limit increases from 3 to 4 glasses, which has a significant impact. --- The LV100 expansion reinforces her identity by rewarding parties that are built around matching elements. If every character other than Wonder starts the battle with the same element, the team gains 20% Pierce. That said, fully matching every party member's element is not especially common, and this buff alone is not enough to overtake the mechanics of newer Elucidator Phantom Thieves released afterward. **The Attack and Critical Damage boosts for other Elucidators granted through Mindscape Amplification are worth prioritizing, because they also improve the stat-scaling support she provides.**

units.review:
Fuuka is a Thief with the unique ability to swap party members using Oracle Shift. Unlike Oracle or Ange, Fuuka provides no Defense down debuffs or pierce rate buffs, so you must be careful with your team composition. At A0, Fuuka generally swaps on rounds 2 and 6. At A6, if there are no extra turns by round 6, she can swap up to 4 times.
**Swap Mechanics Summary** - After selecting Fuuka in the party menu, you can select 1 character not in the party as her Shift Member for Oracle Shift - When using Oracle Shift, the acting [Current Character] become inactive, the Shift Member become active and take 1 action. After this action, the Shift Member become inactive, and the [Current Character] become active to continue their turn.
**Buff Interactions** 1. When a [Current Character] is replaced by the Shift Member, all buffs except those the [Current Character] applied to themselves are copied to the Shift Member. - Self buffs from the [Current Character] and Shift Member are not copied. 2. Similarly, when the Shift Member become inactive and the [Current Character] become active, no buffs are copied. 3. When the Shift Member end their action, decrease the duration of the copied buff by 1 turn. - Example: When Wonder received a buff from Turbo (2 turns) + Rebellion (3 turns), and Fuuka swap Wonder with Chord - Chord will only copies Turbo's buffs (Rebellion is not copied because it is a self buff on Wonder) - Chord uses Turbo HIGHLIGHT (2 turns) - Fuuka swaps Wonder back → Turbo HIGHLIGHT is not copied, Wonder has Turbo buff + Rebellion.
**Shift Member Interactions** 1. Most passives and Talents are not active when the Shift Member is inactive. (treated similarly to faint) 2. Effects that require the Shift Member active will also not work. - Example: When Mitsuru is inactive, [Cruel Edge] will not activate even if allies attack foes with [Frost]. - Example: When Blitz is inactive, her passive that increases Attack when allies attack downed foes will not activate. 3. However, **debuff effects that are from the Shift Member will work**. - Example: The critical damage taken debuff from Mitsuru's Awareness 2

units.review:
Hatsune Miku is an Elucidator Thief released simultaneously on all servers for the global server's 1st anniversary. The additional effects of Feel the Beat (Skill 1) and Clear Sound (Skill 2) change depending on the song currently playing. Each time a song is played, Miku gains the Track that corresponds to that song. For each of the three songs, only one of Skill 1 or Skill 2 can have its effect active, so her rotation changes depending on the party, such as whether Critical Rate or Pierce is needed more.

Foes unable to act · Allies act for 2 turns · Reactivates all 3 Track effects · Critical Damage Up · SP Recovery


**Virtual Concert** Showstopper (Skill 3) is her core skill, spending 3 different Tracks to activate Virtual Concert. When activated, **foes' turns stop and allies gain 2 combat turns**. When Miku enters Virtual Concert, buffs granted by Miku have their duration extended by 2 turns. Because of this, if Skill 1 and Skill 2 are not both used during the 2 turns immediately before Skill 3, one of the base buffs will be missing and efficiency drops sharply. Also, because foes do not act, **debuffs applied to foes remain active during those 2 turns without their turn count decreasing**. If Miku has Awareness 2, all buff effects from Skill 1 and Skill 2 are granted for 2 turns when Virtual Concert is activated. However, turns outside Virtual Concert remain the same, so Awareness 2 does not remove the meaning of her rotation.
**Comparison with Manaka** Since most damage dealers follow a 2-turn damage cycle, Miku is directly compared with Manaka's Turn Revert as a way to gain one additional damage window. Because all allies gain extra turns, and because sub-DPS party members can also benefit, **her basic mechanism is generally considered a stronger version than Manaka's**. However, **Manaka's Turn Revert preserves stacks built up by the damage dealer**, so Manaka can still be stronger for damage dealers that concentrate stacks into one powerful hit on a specific turn, or for damage dealers that require a 3-turn setup. --- **Server Difference** On the KR/CN/TW servers, Sync Mindscape is applied first, greatly increasing Miku's skill values. The EN/JP/SEA global version is expected to receive Sync Mindscape as future versions progress, so even with the same rotation, the current buff values and practical performance feel lower than the KR/CN/TW version. Therefore, on global servers, the rotation structure itself can be referenced as-is, but actual peak performance should be judged separately based on base skill values, signature weapon, and Awareness level.
